tour.markdown:
# Architecture tour: digitalme

Written by `udebt tour` at `f93102b1` on 2026-11-15; 12 units, about 11 minutes to read. Units come in the order to learn them: each after the units it uses.

Digital Me (YPai) is a public chatbot that answers as its owner, Yusuf Pisan, using a persona written as markdown files. A React/Vite frontend on Netlify talks directly to a FastAPI backend on Render. The Chat request lifecycle (SSE) streams each reply, drawing on Persona prompt and retrieval modes and on Safety checks, while Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering bound the Claude spend and Auth and role-based access gates admin features. SQLite persistence stores everything durable. Around that core sit the FAQ cache and voice replies, Email correspondence and notifications, the Contacts database with privacy filter, the Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop, and the Content pipeline and CI/deploy, which uses Git pull requests as its approval gate.

## The map

*Uses*: its code imports the other unit's (strongest first). *Used by*: how many units import it. *Changes with*: the units commits most often touch with it.

1. **Auth and role-based access** (`auth-rbac`): used by 3; changes with `admin-persona-fix-loop`, `frontend-spa`
2. **Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering** (`cost-control`): uses `auth-rbac`; used by 7; changes with `email-notifications`, `analytics-persistence`
3. **Persona prompt and retrieval modes** (`persona-retrieval`): uses `cost-control`; used by 5; changes with `content-pipeline`, `cost-control`
4. **Chat request lifecycle (SSE)** (`chat-flow`): uses `cost-control`, `persona-retrieval`; used by 1; changes with `frontend-spa`, `cost-control`
5. **SQLite persistence (analytics.db) and backup** (`analytics-persistence`): uses `cost-control`; used by 1; changes with `cost-control`, `frontend-spa`
6. **Safety: hostile pre-check, guardrails, bans** (`safety-guardrails`): uses `cost-control`, `persona-retrieval`; used by 1; changes with `persona-retrieval`, `frontend-spa`
7. **Content pipeline and CI/deploy** (`content-pipeline`): used by 1; changes with `persona-retrieval`, `frontend-spa`
8. **FAQ cache and voice replies** (`faq-cache-tts`): uses `persona-retrieval`, `safety-guardrails`, `content-pipeline`, `cost-control`; used by 1; changes with `frontend-spa`, `admin-persona-fix-loop`
9. **Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop** (`admin-persona-fix-loop`): uses `cost-control`, `faq-cache-tts`, `persona-retrieval`, `analytics-persistence`; changes with `frontend-spa`, `cost-control`
10. **React/Vite frontend** (`frontend-spa`): uses `chat-flow`, `auth-rbac`; changes with `admin-persona-fix-loop`, `chat-flow`
11. **Email correspondence and notifications** (`email-notifications`): uses `persona-retrieval`, `auth-rbac`, `cost-control`; changes with `cost-control`, `frontend-spa`
12. **Contacts database with privacy filter** (`contacts-db`): changes with `persona-retrieval`, `email-notifications`

## 1. Auth and role-based access (`auth-rbac`)

This unit lets people sign in with Google, optionally, and decides who may reach admin features. It is used by Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering, Email correspondence and notifications, and the React/Vite frontend. It changes together with the Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop, the frontend and the Chat request lifecycle. The decision: a Google token is exchanged for a signed token that the browser keeps in local storage and sends in a request header, with no cookies. Roles sit in SQLite and are looked up on every request, so changes apply at once. Cookie sessions, an outside auth provider and a fixed admin list were passed over, because the frontend and backend live on different origins. Yusuf Pisan wrote it alone [human], from May through July 2026.

Open first: `backend/roles.py`, `backend/main.py`, `frontend/src/auth.js`.

## 2. Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering (`cost-control`)

This unit keeps Claude spend bounded on a public bot running on the owner's personal key. It uses Auth and role-based access. It is used by the Chat request lifecycle (SSE), Safety, Persona prompt and retrieval modes, the Admin dashboard, FAQ cache and voice replies, SQLite persistence and Email correspondence, and it changes with the persistence, email and frontend units. The decision is layered: per-minute and per-session rate limits, daily exchange caps, token and monthly dollar caps with a point where login becomes required, an exemption for visitors bringing their own key, and metering of the cheap side calls. No limits, a paid-only gate and a flat quota were not chosen; the history says only that the changes were cost-driven. Yusuf Pisan built it across three commits from May to June 2026, all with an AI co-author [assisted].

Open first: `backend/usage_tracker.py`, `backend/main.py`, `backend/analytics.py`.

## 3. Persona prompt and retrieval modes (`persona-retrieval`)

This unit builds the system prompt from the persona markdown files and tone settings, and decides how much persona context each request receives. It uses Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering. It is used by FAQ cache and voice replies, Email correspondence and notifications, the Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop, the Chat request lifecycle (SSE) and Safety. It changes with the Content pipeline, cost controls and the frontend. The decision: persona knowledge stays as plain files in git, and six retrieval modes can be switched at runtime, with cascading as the default. A database setting beats an environment setting, which beats the code default. Fine-tuning, one fixed full prompt and a vector database service were not chosen, since the full persona costs about 40K tokens per call. Yusuf Pisan added the files alone [human] in May 2026, then built the modes and the June refactor with an AI co-author [assisted].

Open first: `persona`, `backend/persona.py`, `backend/cascading.py`.

## 4. Chat request lifecycle (SSE) (`chat-flow`)

This unit handles each chat message, streaming the persona's reply to the browser while it is generated. It uses Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering and Persona prompt and retrieval modes. The React/Vite frontend uses it, and it changes together with the frontend, cost controls and the Admin dashboard. The decision: one async endpoint streams server-sent events. A cheap hostile pre-check runs first, then retrieval and model choice, then a hard sentence cap. Guardrail and follow-up calls run concurrently afterward, and history is saved even if the client disconnects. WebSockets, blocking requests and a worker queue were not chosen, for latency and a free event loop. Yusuf Pisan wrote the first version alone [human] in May 2026, reworked it with an AI co-author [assisted] in June, and hardened it alone [human] in July after real failures.

Open first: `backend/main.py`, `backend/sentences.py`, `frontend/src/sse.js`.

## 5. SQLite persistence (analytics.db) and backup (`analytics-persistence`)

This unit is the system of record: one SQLite file on Render's persistent disk holding conversations, users and roles, bans, feedback, proposals, usage and settings. It uses Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering, and it is used by the Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop. It changes together with cost controls, the frontend and the admin dashboard. The decision: a single file with schema migrations in code, with chat context rebuilt from it by session id, plus a daily compressed snapshot pushed to a private GitHub repository as protection against disk loss. Postgres, a managed database and browser or cookie session state were not chosen; the stated reason is simplicity and low cost for one owner. The history shows Yusuf Pisan wrote it alone [human] between May and July 2026.

Open first: `backend/analytics.py`, `backend/backup.py`, `scripts/backup_db.py`.

## 6. Safety: hostile pre-check, guardrails, bans (`safety-guardrails`)

This unit classifies each incoming message and checks each reply, with strikes and bans that persist. It uses Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering and Persona prompt and retrieval modes. FAQ cache and voice replies use it. It changes with the persona unit, the frontend, which shows the warmth meter, and the Chat request lifecycle. The decision: a small Haiku model screens messages for hostile or manipulative input, three strikes or a 24-hour ban follow, and bans are tied to a stable visitor identity stored in SQLite. The reply check fails closed, and the sentence limit is enforced on the server. Prompt-only rules, IP bans and third-party moderation were not chosen, because prompts were evaded and bans must survive redeploys. Fingerprinting was rejected for privacy. Yusuf Pisan introduced it with an AI co-author [assisted] in May 2026 and extended it alone [human] in June.

Open first: `backend/hostile.py`, `backend/guardrails.py`, `backend/visitor.py`.

## 7. Content pipeline and CI/deploy (`content-pipeline`)

This unit turns scored headlines into drafted posts and ships the code. It is used by FAQ cache and voice replies, and it changes together with Persona prompt and retrieval modes, the frontend and the Admin dashboard. The decision: Git is the approval and ingestion mechanism. A GitHub Action or local command-line tool drafts a post as a pull request, merging ingests it, and a gated Render deploy follows. CI checks lint, types, tests and the build. A content management system, direct publishing and manual deploys were not chosen, since pull requests keep a human in control. The daily cron was disabled in June 2026 to stop unmetered API spend. Yusuf Pisan built the pipeline alone [human] in May, added typing, CI gates and the cron change with an AI co-author [assisted] in June, and added auto-deploy alone [human] in July.

Open first: `automation`, `posts`, `.github/workflows`.

## 8. FAQ cache and voice replies (`faq-cache-tts`)

This unit serves pre-generated answers to common questions without a full model call, and can attach ElevenLabs audio. It uses Persona prompt and retrieval modes, Safety, Content pipeline and CI/deploy, and Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering. The Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop use it, and it changes with the frontend, the dashboard and the Chat request lifecycle. The decision: entries are served stale while they refresh, keyed to a hash of the persona and written using the shorter distilled persona. Audio clips are stored on disk under a hash of the answer text. Regenerating the whole bank on every deploy, or tracking audio in a manifest or database column, were not chosen; one regeneration cost about $5, and hashing orphans old clips automatically. Yusuf Pisan began it with an AI co-author [assisted] in May 2026, worked on it alone [human] through June, and added voice replies with an AI co-author [assisted] in July.

Open first: `backend/faq_cache.py`, `backend/tts.py`, `backend/data/faq_cache.json`.

## 9. Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop (`admin-persona-fix-loop`)

This unit lets admins review conversations and rate replies, then turns that feedback into proposed persona edits delivered as a GitHub pull request. It uses Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering, FAQ cache and voice replies, Persona prompt and retrieval modes, and SQLite persistence. It changes with the frontend, cost controls and persistence. The decision: feedback goes to Sonnet, which returns whole-file rewrites. A background thread does the work while the client polls, because synchronous generation timed out at the edge proxy. Edits are limited to an allowlist of persona files and open a pull request rather than pushing to main, so a human approves. Manual edits and a job queue were not chosen. Yusuf Pisan introduced it in May 2026 with an AI co-author [assisted], then extended the admin page and sessions alone [human] in late May and June.

Open first: `frontend/src/AdminPage.jsx`, `backend/repo_admin.py`, `backend/faq_gap_report.py`.

## 10. React/Vite frontend (`frontend-spa`)

This unit is the browser app: chat, the admin page, shared conversation views and the warmth meter, installable as a PWA and hosted on Netlify. It uses the Chat request lifecycle (SSE) and Auth and role-based access, and it changes together with the Admin dashboard, the chat lifecycle and cost controls. The decision: plain React in JavaScript with type checking through documentation comments, local storage for the token, session resume and visitor id, and direct calls to Render with restricted CORS and no proxy. Next.js server rendering, a Netlify proxy and cookies were not chosen, given the cross-origin deploy and the wish for a simple static host. Yusuf Pisan wrote most of it alone [human], including the July hardening and the September avatars and home-screen support, with an AI co-author [assisted] adding type checking in June.

Open first: `frontend`.

## 11. Email correspondence and notifications (`email-notifications`)

This unit handles inbound mail through Resend, approval-gated draft replies and notification emails. It uses Persona prompt and retrieval modes, Auth and role-based access, and Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering. It changes together with cost controls, the frontend and the persona unit. The decision: inbound mail is stored in threads, drafts are generated only when an admin clicks, and sending needs explicit approval. The notifier emails people who hold the relevant capability and throttles API-key alerts using a timestamp in the database. Auto-reply, the Gmail API and plain SMTP were not chosen, to prevent spam and cost and keep a human gate. The features stay inert without environment configuration. Yusuf Pisan wrote it alone [human] in late May and early June 2026, and the history does not say more about the choice of Resend.

Open first: `backend/email_agent.py`, `backend/notifier.py`, `backend/email_topics.md`.

## 12. Contacts database with privacy filter (`contacts-db`)

This unit looks up contacts on demand from a separate contacts database and injects the result into prompts only for that request. Nothing in the listed connections uses it directly; it changes together with Persona prompt and retrieval modes, Email correspondence and notifications, and Cost controls. The decision: a separate SQLite file is built offline from email and LinkedIn data by scripts, a privacy filter drops personal-email and family contacts, and the file is copied to the Render disk. Putting contacts in persona files, or skipping lookup, were not chosen, because the data is large, about 18K entries, and private, so it stays out of both the prompt and git. The history shows only a June 2026 documentation commit by Yusuf Pisan with an AI co-author [assisted], recording a privacy rebuild and production deploy; earlier authorship is not shown.

Open first: `backend/contacts.py`, `scripts/populate_contacts_db.py`, `scripts/parse_email_contacts.py`.

---

Next: `udebt path` for the order to learn these in and the time each takes, `udebt dig <unit>` for a walkthrough of one with its code.

chat-flow.flow: A visitor types a question in the chat box and the browser POSTs it to /api/chat, then renders the streamed reply as it arrives and gets a final "done" event.

steps.narration: The browser starts the request with an AbortController and a 60-second watchdog that re-arms whenever bytes arrive. Part of Yusuf Pisan's July hardening commit [human] added it: an idle socket never errors on its own, so without it the typing dots could spin forever. The Stop button uses the same controller, and aborting is what the server later sees as a disconnect.

Inside the generator, before any model call, a cheap Haiku hostile check runs on the message. If it flags the message, strikes are recorded and the penalty is applied. The branches that follow either send a short in-voice reply, send nothing, or ban, and each ends the stream early. This is why the user turn is already in history at this point, and why each early exit has to keep history consistent.

After retrieval and model selection, the stream opens on the async client. Each text delta passes through the sentence streamer, then PII scrubbing and control-tag stripping, and only then becomes an SSE 'chunk' event. Because the client is async and each chunk is yielded as it arrives, the event loop stays free for other visitors. That was the point of the June async refactor [assisted].

The streamer releases text only up to completed sentence boundaries and holds the partial tail. When the tier's max_sentences is reached it cuts at that boundary and sets a permanent capped flag. The cap is enforced on the server by counting terminators, so it holds even if the model ignores the prompt or answers in another language. The tail flush at stream end (flush_complete or flush_truncated) respects the same flag.

Once the reply is stored, the guardrail check and the follow-up generation are two independent Haiku calls. They run through asyncio.gather so the 'done' event, which carries the follow-up chips and the message counter, waits for one round trip instead of two. This is the 'slow done event' fix. The guardrail runs after delivery, so it records violations and adjusts trust but cannot block a reply that has already been sent.

If the client disconnects, Starlette cancels the generator at its current await or yield. The handler repairs the in-memory history synchronously. It keeps a partial reply recorded with mode 'aborted' if any text was delivered, and otherwise pops the unanswered user turn. A dangling user turn would make the Messages API reject every later send in that session with a 400. The code then re-raises so cancellation still propagates.

chat-flow.trap: A reader may think the guardrail check screens the reply before the user sees it, but it runs only after the full reply has streamed, so it records violations and adjusts trust and cannot block anything. Real-time protection comes only from the persona rules, the PII scrub and the pre-send hostile check.
